questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I always knew that I wanted to go to USA on exchange, but I wasn't sure where. The reason why Texas was a destination I wanted to go to, was because I hadn't been there before and wanted to explore new culture and opportunities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult to begin with. Many of the other faculties, Law especially, were very good at informing their new students on how to get started with applying for classes and so on. Liberal Arts, which I was attached to, didn't inform me of anything.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not a lot unfortunately. The school should have been better at helping new students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was difficult to find affordable housing. A lot of the houses were way too expensive, but I just stumbled upon a place on google, which helped me find a place.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I will 100 % recommend living on West Campus. It's a place where most of the students live, which means the average age is around 20 of all the people living there.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult, but I managed to find a guy who helped me out.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was possible to contact the department, in my case Liberal Arts, who assigned someone to help you on Zoom.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted, and the school made sure I got them.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Contact the department your attached to. They will make sure someone helps you out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level is lower and made in a different way than what I was used to. It seems more like a "high school" level compared to Economics in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In Copenhagen, the professors have lectures with 100-300 students at the same time. At University of Texas, the classes were much smaller with maybe 10-30 students. It seemed almost like being back in "gymnasium".

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to Game Theory
Innovation & Entrepreneurship
Philosophy of Science
The Eco of Money - From past to Bitcoin

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: N/A

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The insurance was mandatory and was on almost 14.000 DKK. It is in my opinion extremely stupid, because it covers less than an insurance from Denmark, that costs 3.000 DKK.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Insurance

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Extremely good! The school really wants their students to socialize and do sports.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The school gives the opportunity to play tennis (20 courts), basket (10 courts), squash (6 courts), racketball (10 courts), soccer (maaany courts), fitness and so on. And everything was free.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Intramural sports - sign up with a team and play your favorite sport in a competition against other students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Cain & Abels, which is the local student bar - they have some nice offers especially on Tuesdays. 
Go Padel/Kayaking on Lady Bird lake.
Go to 6th Street in the evening, where they have some nice bars/clubs. Go to Rainey Street and enjoy a nice microbrewed beer.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, there are many pleasant and nice people who will help you out.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: As mentioned go to Cain & Abels - it will help a lot. ;-)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It seems like Austin is quite like Europe - very young and liberal people. So it isn't what you read about, when hearing about Texas.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The young society.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Enjoy it, before you look around it's already over.
2. Even though it's extremely warm during summer, pack a jacket for the winter, which actually gets quite cold. 
3. Live on West Campus!! It's a must.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The social environment. Some nice new friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Combining alcohol with going to classes.. ;-)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
